kinds.d: Cleaned real skull of a mammal kept as a specimen. Legality varies; protected species and CITES listings restrict trade.

x.d: Flesh removed by dermestid beetles, then whitened with hydrogen peroxide; the museum and professional method.
Skull mounted on a plaque, with or without horns; boiling is the traditional method.

kinds.d: Cleaned real skull of a bird kept as a specimen. Wild-bird parts are restricted by migratory-bird laws.

x.d: Small bird skulls cleaned by dermestid beetles.

kinds.d: Cleaned real skull of a reptile (alligator, turtle, snake, lizard) kept as a specimen.
Cleaned real skull of a bony fish kept as a specimen. A dried jaw or tooth set is under Fish jaw or teeth set.
Real animal skeleton, cleaned and articulated on a stand or in a case.

x.d: Articulated skeletons shown at the Oklahoma City museum, including a humpback whale (one of twelve fully articulated in North America) and a Javan rhinoceros.

kinds.d: Cast copy of a skull or fossil in resin, such as hominid skulls; a replica, not a real specimen.

x.d: 1:1 polyurethane resin cast of Australopithecus afarensis, supplied by Bone Clones.
x.dt: 1:1 scale · two-part cranium and jaw · tar or antique finish

x.d: Set of nine casts: Homo habilis, Peking Man, Mrs Ples, La Chapelle Neanderthal, Nariokotome boy, Zinjanthropus, Taung Child, Kenyanthropus and Lucy.

brands.d: Oklahoma City supplier of real and replica skulls and skeletons, with beetle cleaning services.
Chatsworth, California maker of polyurethane casts of skulls and skeletons, including hominid fossils.

notes: Reptile and fish skulls kept with old sources and type lists only. Deer, bear, beaver, alligator, piranha archetypes not sourced on retrieved pages so given as types.
